head: About 20% of all bitcoin [is lost.]
sub: Lost phones. Lost seed phrases. No plan for family.
vo: Lose your phone, or your seed phrase, and your crypto is gone. Pass away without a plan, and your family never sees it. About a fifth of all bitcoin is already lost this way.

head: A vault [with a latch.]
sub: Check in now and then. Go quiet, and it opens for the address you named.
vo: Latchkey is a vault with a latch. You check in now and then. If you go quiet for too long, it opens for the address you named: your own backup wallet, or the person you love.

head: Set it up [in a minute.]
sub: Receiver, silence window, grace period, up to three guardians.
vo: Setting one up takes a minute. Name who it opens for, how long a silence means something is wrong, a grace period, and up to three guardians. Then fund it from any wallet. You keep the keys, and you can take everything back while it's open.

head: One tap: [I’m still here.]
sub: Every check-in is one beat of a TapeOut circuit on X Layer.
vo: Checking in is one tap. Every check-in is a beat of a TapeOut circuit on X Layer, and the vault keeps each beat on chain.

head: The latch [is a chip.]
sub: 18 NAND + 2 LATCH, built by REF on a 2-of-3 guardian circuit.
vo: The latch isn't a flag in our database. It's a circuit taped out on TapeOut: two latch bits and eighteen NAND gates, built by REF on top of a second circuit that counts guardian votes. Your browser checks all two hundred and fifty six cases against the processor, live. Once it trips, it can never be undone.

head: Go quiet, [and it opens.]
sub: Grace period, TapeSend notice, two guardians confirm, the bit flips.
vo: Now I stop checking in. When the window runs out, anyone can start the grace period, and Latchkey's herald sends a TapeSend message from its own container. Two guardians confirm. The circuit flips the bit, and my heir gets a TapeSend message of their own.

head: Your heir [claims.]
sub: Only the named wallet. No company, no keeper, no paperwork.
vo: My heir connects the wallet I named, and claims everything to their own wallet. No company, no keeper, no paperwork.

head: Built to [outlive us.]
sub: No admin over funds. Notices on TapeSend. The app itself on DeWEB.
vo: Inheritance apps are companies, and companies shut down. Latchkey has no admin over your funds, its notices travel over TapeSend, and the app itself is one file stored on X Layer DeWEB, served from its own dot tape name. It can't disappear before you do.

head: Free to start. [Paid when it matters.]
sub: 0.001 OKB setup · 0.2% at claim · optional watchtower reminders.
vo: Setup costs a thousandth of an OKB, about ten cents, and Latchkey takes zero point two percent only when a vault pays out. An optional watchtower adds reminders. We're starting with the eighty percent of Nigerian crypto users who save in dollars.
